seo.title: Wine Bars in Thessaloniki (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the best wine bars in Thessaloniki for 2026 — curated picks with maps, hours, and insider tips.

hero.h1: Taste northern Greek wines and ouzo pairings at Thessaloniki wine bars
hero.subtitle: Thessaloniki's vibrant culinary scene offers an incredible journey through Northern Greek wines and spirited ouzo, perfectly paired with delicious local mezedes.

picks.name: Oinovate
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Oinovate is a contemporary wine bar offering an extensive list focusing heavily on Greek vineyards, especially from the North. Its chic, industrial-minimalist design provides a sophisticated backdrop for enjoying rare vintages and popular labels alongside creative meze dishes designed to complement the wine. The staff are highly knowledgeable and passionate.
picks.whatToOrder: A flight of indigenous Northern Greek wines (e.g., Xinomavro, Malagousia) paired with their truffle mushroom pie or cured meat platter.
picks.insiderTip: Ask the sommelier for off-menu recommendations or newly arrived local labels; they often have unique finds not yet on the main list.
picks.redditQuote: "Oinovate is a must for any wine lover in Thessaloniki. The Xinomavro selection is insane, and their truffle pie? Forget about it. Best spot for a date night too."

picks.name: Vogatsikou 3
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Nestled in a charming street, Vogatsikou 3 is an elegant wine bar and restaurant known for its refined atmosphere and a deep cellar of Greek and international wines. It expertly blends traditional Greek flavors with modern culinary techniques, offering a sophisticated dining experience where each dish is crafted to enhance its wine pairing. Expect impeccable service and a cozy yet upscale ambiance.
picks.whatToOrder: Their slow-cooked lamb with a robust Xinomavro from Naoussa or Amyntaio, followed by a local cheese board.
picks.insiderTip: Reservations are highly recommended, especially on weekends, as it's a popular spot for locals seeking a high-quality wine and dining experience.
picks.redditQuote: "Vogatsikou 3 feels like a hidden gem, even though it's super popular. The wine pairings are always spot-on, and their lamb is probably the best I've had in Greece."

picks.name: The Aficionados
picks.whyItMadeTheList: More than just a wine bar, The Aficionados is a dedicated temple to Greek wines, functioning as both a boutique wine shop and a tasting spot. It’s perfect for those who want to delve deep into the nuances of Greek viticulture. They host regular tasting events and offer expert guidance, making it an educational and enjoyable experience to discover unique local producers.
picks.whatToOrder: Participate in a guided tasting session featuring wines from different Northern Greek regions, accompanied by a small platter of artisanal cheeses and charcuterie.
picks.insiderTip: Keep an eye on their social media for special tasting events or guest winemakers, which offer a unique opportunity to learn directly from the source.
picks.redditQuote: "If you're serious about Greek wines, The Aficionados is your spot. They have such a knowledgeable staff and you can try some really obscure but amazing bottles. Highly recommend their tasting events!"

picks.name: Mezen (Μέζεν)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Mezen offers a modern take on the traditional tsipouradiko, specializing in tsipouro and ouzo served alongside a dazzling array of creative and fresh mezedes. While their focus is on spirits, they understand the art of pairing, and their dishes elevate the ouzo experience beyond simple bites. It's a lively and popular spot, great for sharing small plates with friends.
picks.whatToOrder: Several rounds of aged tsipouro or ouzo, paired with their grilled octopus, 'soutzoukakia' (spicy meatballs), and smoked mackerel salad.
picks.insiderTip: Mezen gets very busy, especially during peak hours. Arrive early for lunch or make a reservation for dinner to secure a good table.
picks.redditQuote: "Mezen's meze are next level, not your average fried stuff. The octopus with ouzo is just perfection. Seriously, don't miss this place if you're into tsipouro and good food."

picks.name: Chilai Wine Bar & Restaurant
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Chilai presents a sleek, contemporary setting for enjoying a curated selection of Greek and international wines. Their menu features innovative Mediterranean dishes with a focus on fresh, seasonal ingredients, making it an excellent choice for a complete culinary experience. It’s a sophisticated spot popular for after-work drinks and elegant dinners.
picks.whatToOrder: A bottle of a full-bodied Greek red (like a Limniona or Agiorgitiko) with their beef tagliata or a seafood pasta, followed by a cheese board.
picks.insiderTip: They often have live jazz or chill music nights, which adds to the sophisticated ambiance. Check their schedule beforehand if you're interested.
picks.redditQuote: "Chilai has such a good vibe and their wine list is solid. The food is also top-notch, especially their pasta dishes. Perfect for a slightly more upscale evening."

picks.name: Mia Feta
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Mia Feta is a delightful haven for cheese lovers, offering an extensive selection of Greek and international cheeses, along with artisanal charcuterie. This charming spot specializes in pairing these savory delights with a carefully chosen array of Greek wines. It's an intimate and cozy setting, perfect for a relaxed evening of tasting and discovery.
picks.whatToOrder: A custom cheese and charcuterie platter featuring local Greek cheeses, paired with a crisp Assyrtiko or a fruity Malagousia.
picks.insiderTip: Don't be afraid to ask for recommendations; the staff are passionate about their cheeses and wines and can guide you to unique combinations.
picks.redditQuote: "Mia Feta is my absolute favorite. The variety of cheeses is incredible, and they always suggest the perfect wine to go with them. Their graviera is a game changer."

picks.name: Dotsi (Δώτση)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located in the historic Ladadika district, Dotsi is a beloved traditional ouzeri that captures the essence of old Thessaloniki. With its rustic decor and lively atmosphere, it’s an ideal place to experience authentic Greek hospitality. They serve a wide variety of ouzo and tsipouro, accompanied by classic, generously portioned meze dishes, making it perfect for a group outing.
picks.whatToOrder: Several shots of ouzo from Lesvos or Plomari, accompanied by fried zucchini, saganaki, and their signature meatballs.
picks.insiderTip: Ladadika comes alive at night, and Dotsi is right in the heart of it. Enjoy the bustling ambiance but be prepared for it to be loud and vibrant.
picks.redditQuote: "Dotsi in Ladadika is classic! You go for the ouzo, stay for the meze. Their fried zucchini is ridiculously good, and the vibe is always buzzing."

picks.name: Loxias (Λοξίας)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Loxias is a popular mezedopoleio known for its hearty, home-style Greek cooking and convivial atmosphere. While not exclusively a wine bar, they offer a good selection of local bulk wine (in carafes) and bottled Greek wines that pair perfectly with their extensive menu of classic meze. It’s a local favorite for a relaxed meal and good conversation.
picks.whatToOrder: A carafe of house red or white wine, paired with their grilled mushrooms, fried small fish (gavros), and a fresh Greek salad.
picks.insiderTip: Portions are generous, so order a few meze to share first and then decide if you need more. Don't over-order!
picks.redditQuote: "Loxias is where the locals go for real food and good vibes. Their house wine is surprisingly decent and goes great with everything. The grilled mushrooms are a must!"

picks.name: Kafeneio 'O Giatros' (Καφενείο 'Ο Γιατρός')
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Perched in the historic Ano Poli, Kafeneio 'O Giatros' offers an authentic glimpse into old Thessaloniki. This charming, unpretentious kafenio is famous for its simple yet delicious meze accompanying generous servings of ouzo and tsipouro. It’s a truly local spot, perfect for soaking in the history and enjoying a relaxed, budget-friendly experience with stunning views.
picks.whatToOrder: Enjoy several rounds of ouzo with accompanying classic meze like olives, feta, bread, and perhaps some small fried fish or local sausages.
picks.insiderTip: Find a table outside for incredible panoramic views of the city, especially beautiful during sunset. It’s a bit of a walk up, but worth it.
picks.redditQuote: "O Giatros in Ano Poli is the real deal. Forget fancy, just good ouzo, simple meze, and the best view in Thessaloniki. It's cheap and cheerful."

picks.name: Paralio (Παράλιο)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located directly on the beautiful Nea Paralia waterfront, Paralio is a fantastic choice for those who love fresh seafood and the refreshing pairing of ouzo. This traditional taverna offers a wide selection of fish and seafood, prepared simply to highlight their natural flavors. The sea breeze and scenic views create a perfect ambiance for a leisurely meal.
picks.whatToOrder: Fresh grilled calamari or sardines with a chilled bottle of ouzo and a crisp white wine like Savatiano or Roditis.
picks.insiderTip: Go during the late afternoon to enjoy a beautiful sunset over the Thermaic Gulf while you dine.
picks.redditQuote: "Paralio is my go-to for seafood and ouzo by the sea. The fried gavros is addictive, and the view is just unbeatable. Perfect for a long, lazy lunch."

picks.name: Nea Folia (Νέα Φωλιά)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Nea Folia is renowned for its authentic, hearty Greek home cooking. While not a dedicated wine bar, they pride themselves on offering excellent local wines that perfectly complement their rich, traditional dishes. It’s a cozy, unpretentious taverna that feels like stepping into a Greek grandmother's kitchen, providing a genuine taste of Greek hospitality.
picks.whatToOrder: Their moussaka or yemista (stuffed vegetables) paired with a robust local red wine served in a carafe.
picks.insiderTip: The menu changes seasonally, so ask about daily specials for the freshest and most authentic options.
picks.redditQuote: "Nea Folia is the definition of comfort food in Thessaloniki. Their moussaka is legendary, and the house wine just makes everything better. It's like eating at your yiayia's house."

picks.name: Salonika Restaurant & Bar (Makedonia Palace)
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located within the iconic Makedonia Palace Hotel, Salonika Restaurant & Bar offers a luxurious experience with breathtaking views of the Thermaic Gulf. It boasts a sophisticated wine list featuring premium Greek and international labels, with a strong emphasis on Northern Greek estates. The innovative menu reinterprets traditional Greek cuisine with elegance, perfect for a special occasion or a high-end tasting.
picks.whatToOrder: A bottle of a prestigious Xinomavro from a top estate, paired with a contemporary Greek dish like sea bass ceviche or slow-cooked veal, enjoyed from their terrace.
picks.insiderTip: Dress code is smart casual. Book a table by the window or on the terrace for the best views, especially around sunset.
picks.redditQuote: "For a fancy night out, Salonika Bar at Makedonia Palace is unbeatable. The views are insane, and they have some really high-end Greek wines you won't find just anywhere. Worth the splurge for sure."

faq.question: What kind of wines should I expect to find in Northern Greece, specifically around Thessaloniki?
faq.answer: Northern Greece is renowned for its diverse wine production. You can expect to find excellent red wines primarily from the Xinomavro grape, known for its high acidity, firm tannins, and complex aromas, especially from regions like Naoussa and Amyntaio. For white wines, look for Malagousia, a fragrant and full-bodied varietal, and Assyrtiko, offering crisp minerality, often found in blends or from vineyards with volcanic soil.

faq.question: What is the typical alcohol content of ouzo and how is it traditionally consumed?
faq.answer: Ouzo typically has an alcohol content ranging from 37.5% to 47% ABV. It is traditionally served neat in a tall, narrow glass, often with a glass of cold water and ice on the side. When water or ice is added, ouzo turns milky white, a phenomenon known as the 'ouzo effect,' due to the anethole in the spirit becoming insoluble. It's usually sipped slowly alongside a variety of mezedes (small appetizers).

faq.question: Are wine tastings commonly offered at Thessaloniki wine bars, or do I need to visit a vineyard?
faq.answer: Yes, many wine bars in Thessaloniki, such as Oinovate and The Aficionados, specifically offer wine tastings, often focusing on Northern Greek varietals. While visiting a vineyard (like Ktima Gerovassiliou, which is a short drive away) offers a different, immersive experience, you can absolutely enjoy comprehensive tastings and expert guidance right within the city's wine bars.

faq.question: What are some common mezedes (appetizers) typically paired with ouzo in Thessaloniki?
faq.answer: Common mezedes served with ouzo in Thessaloniki include fresh seafood like grilled octopus, fried calamari, or small fried fish (gavros or sardines). Other popular options are saganaki (fried cheese), tzatziki, olives, feta cheese, various cold cuts (like pastourma), meatballs, and fried zucchini. The variety is vast, designed to complement the anise flavor of the ouzo.

faq.question: What is the price range for a good glass of Northern Greek wine or a serving of ouzo in Thessaloniki?
faq.answer: The price range can vary significantly depending on the venue and the specific wine or ouzo. For a good glass of Northern Greek wine at a quality wine bar, expect to pay €6-10 ($6.50-11). A serving of ouzo, often accompanied by a small meze, typically costs €4-8 ($4.30-8.60). Upscale venues and premium labels will naturally command higher prices.

faq.question: Is it customary to tip in Thessaloniki wine bars and ouzeris, and if so, how much?
faq.answer: Tipping in Greece is appreciated but not strictly mandatory like in some other countries. For good service at a wine bar or ouzeri, it's customary to round up the bill or leave a small tip, typically 5-10% of the total, especially if you've had an excellent experience. For very casual places, simply rounding up to the nearest euro is sufficient.
